subject: Next steps: tenant segmentation & deployment requirements for Lumina POC
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@luminaai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: tenant segmentation & deployment requirements for Lumina POC

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the POC scope (focus: data isolation expectations and deployment mode).

Recap (short):
- Lumina’s primary concern: strict tenant-level separation for customer data and auditability for SOC2-style evidence.
- Two candidate deployment modes we discussed: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools, logical tenancy) vs Redwood Private (VPC/private control plane).
- Key technical asks from your side: encrypted separation at rest + transit, dedicated KMS integration, network egress controls, and evidence of audit logs retention.

Immediate questions we flagged on the call (we need answers to size the POC):
- Is Lumina willing to run the POC in our Dedicated environment if we provide strict tenant segmentation + customer-managed KMS? (This would be faster to stand up.)
- Or do you require a Private VPC (VPC peering or on-prem) for the POC due to procurement/regulatory constraints?

Proposed next steps:
1) Lumina: confirm required deployment mode for POC by Tue 20 Apr (dedicated with CMK vs Private VPC).
2) Redwood: if Dedicated accepted, Ben will share a short one-page network/segmentation diagram and KMS integration notes (attached).
3) If Private required, Marissa will schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive next week to capture VPC peering/firewall and on-prem checklist items.
4) Both sides: exchange a minimal evidence pack for SOC2-related items (audit log fields, retention window).

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-network-diagram.pdf (network + tenant isolation), vpc-isolation-checklist.xlsx (questions for your infra team), POC-MAP-2027-04.docx (timeline draft).

Proposed timeline: agree mode by Tue 20 Apr -> perf/security run-through Wed/Thu -> POC kickoff week of Apr 26.

If you prefer a quick call instead of the doc exchange, I’m free Mon 19 Apr 10–11am PDT.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Direct: (415) 555-0142

---
On Sun, 18 Apr 2027 at 12:40 PM, Alex Wu <alex.wu@luminaai.com> wrote:
> Thanks Jordan — great presentation. I’ll pull together our infra owner (Nisha) to confirm whether Reserved/Dedicated meets procurement. If not, we’ll need Private VPC for the POC.
> 
> A couple of clarifications:
> - Encryption: we need BYOK/KMS with customer key owners and separate key per environment.
> - Audit logs: at least 90 days of immutable access logs; ideally replayable query on call traces.
> - Network: strict egress controls; no public internet access from model serving.
> 
> I’ll confirm by Tue.
> —Alex
From: Nisha Patel <nisha.patel@luminaai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Wu <alex.wu@luminaai.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: tenant segmentation & deployment requirements for Lumina POC

Jordan — thanks for the clear summary. Short answers from infra/security:
- We prefer Private VPC for the POC because procurement needs to validate network isolation with our MSP and we need control-plane access to run some compliance checks.
- That said, if Redwood can provide a documented set of controls and a temporary CMK-based Dedicated setup with documented immutable logs and no egress, procurement may accept it for the quick pilot. Decision will be final after we see the checklist.

Action items from our side: I’ll run the vpc-isolation-checklist.xlsx with our platform ops and get back by EOD Tue 20 Apr.

Thanks — Nisha
Nisha Patel
Infrastructure Lead, Lumina AI
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Nisha Patel <nisha.patel@luminaai.com>, Alex Wu <alex.wu@luminaai.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: tenant segmentation & deployment requirements for Lumina POC

Hi Nisha / Alex — quick technical clarifications to help procurement triage:
- Dedicated option: provides strict logical tenant segmentation. Each Lumina tenant would run in a dedicated namespace with RBAC isolation, disk-level AES-256 encryption, and optional per-tenant CMKs via KMS import. Network egress can be locked down with a customer-specific egress rule set (no public outbound by default). See attached diagram for flow.
- Private VPC option: provides network-level isolation (VPC peering or PrivateLink), customer-managed VPN, and an on-prem package if required. Control plane endpoints can be restricted to your IP allowlist and integrated with your SSO/SAML.
- Audit logs: we can provide append-only access logs for the POC with 90-day retention; we also offer a long-term archival option to your S3 bucket for compliance.

If you’d like, Marissa and I can run an infra-to-infra session this week to walk the checklist in your environment (30–45 min).

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@luminaai.com>, Nisha Patel <nisha.patel@luminaai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: tenant segmentation & deployment requirements for Lumina POC

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Nisha. Sounds like we have a clear path:
- Lumina will validate the checklist today.
- If procurement accepts Dedicated with CMK + immutable logs + egress controls, we’ll proceed on Dedicated for the POC (faster).
- Otherwise, we’ll schedule the Private VPC deep-dive (Marissa to propose times).

Marissa — can you propose two 30–45 min slots Thu 22 Apr (10:00–11:00 PDT or 14:00–15:00 PDT) for the infra-to-infra session assuming Private is required? Also please attach the short control-matrix that procurement can review (one pager).

Alex / Nisha — thanks again. Jordan
